results.outcome: Mortality at longest follow-up (60-day mortality / survival)
results.numerical_result: 60-day mortality 20/54 (study group) vs 28/51 (control group); Kaplan-Meier HR = 0.565, 95% CI 0.320-0.999, P = 0.046 (28-day mortality 15/54 vs 23/51, P = 0.065)
results.result_location: p. 1410, Section 3.5 'Prognostic analysis' (deaths by cause: 20 study vs 28 control) and p. 1411, Figure 1 (Kaplan-Meier curve with numbers at risk); 28-day mortality in p. 1410, Table 5

1.1.support: Random assignment of patients into either the control group or the study group was performed using a random number table.

1.2.support: The report describes only a random number table for sequence generation; I looked for any description of allocation concealment (sealed opaque envelopes, central or remote allocation) in the methods and found none.

1.3.support: They presented a homogeneous profile (all P > 0.05). Table 1 lists between-group P values of 0.426, 0.252, 0.234, 0.672, 0.216, 0.226 and 0.441 for the baseline characteristics.
1.3.location: p. 1409, Table 1 and Section 3.2 Baseline characteristics

2.1.support: I looked for any statement that participants were blinded to, or aware of, the assigned PEEP-titration strategy and found none; the report says only that both groups received sedation.

2.2.support: The study group underwent PEEP titration based on transpulmonary driving pressure. Esophageal pressure was measured as a surrogate for pleural pressure using an esophageal pressure measurement catheter connected to the ventilator; no blinding of carers or clinicians is described.

2.3.support: The report describes no deviations from the assigned PEEP-titration strategy, no crossovers between groups and no non-adherence in either group; I found no evidence that trial context changed what participants received.

2.4.support: Conditional on 2.3; 2.3 was answered PN, so this question is not applicable.

2.5.support: Conditional on 2.4; 2.4 was answered NA, so this question is not applicable.

2.6.support: Comparison of 28-day mortality, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of hospital stay, and incidence of VAP between the two patient groups revealed that in the control group, 23 patients died within 28 days, with a total of 16 cases of VAP; all outcomes in Table 5 are reported for all 51 control and 54 study participants.

2.7.support: Conditional on 2.6; 2.6 was answered Y, so this question is not applicable.

3.1.support: All patients were followed up for 60 days after discharge to record their survival status; Figure 1 accounts for all 51 control and 54 study participants (28 and 20 deaths, matching the numbers at risk at day 60 of 23 and 34).
3.1.location: p. 1408, Section 2.4.4; p. 1410, Section 3.5; p. 1411, Figure 1

3.2.support: Conditional on 3.1; 3.1 was answered Y, so this question is not applicable.

3.3.support: Conditional on 3.2; 3.2 was answered NA, so this question is not applicable.

3.4.support: Conditional on 3.3; 3.3 was answered NA, so this question is not applicable.

4.1.support: Survival status was recorded by follow-up of all patients ('All patients were followed up for 60 days after discharge to record their survival status'); I found no indication that mortality was ascertained with an insensitive or invalid method.

4.2.support: I looked for any difference between the groups in the method, timing or intensity of outcome ascertainment (for example additional monitoring or detection opportunities) and found none; both groups were managed and followed identically.

4.3.support: No blinding of outcome assessors is described; the treating clinicians and investigators who recorded deaths and survival status knew the assigned ventilation strategy.

4.4.support: Death is an objective, unambiguous event and I found no judgement-based component in its ascertainment; knowledge of the assigned ventilation strategy cannot influence whether a patient is recorded as having died.

4.5.support: Conditional on 4.4; 4.4 was answered N, so this question is not applicable.

5.1.support: I looked for a trial protocol, statistical analysis plan or registry record, or any statement that the analysis plan was finalised before unblinded outcome data were available, and found none in the report.

5.2.support: Analysis intentions are not available, and mortality is one of several eligible ways in which this outcome domain could have been measured (28-day mortality is reported in Table 5 whereas 60-day survival is reported in Figure 1).

5.3.support: Analysis intentions are not available, and the mortality data could have been analysed in multiple eligible ways (crude between-group proportions with chi-square, as in Table 5, versus the Cox model/Kaplan-Meier analysis reported for 60-day survival).
5.3.location: p. 1410, Section 3.5 and Table 5; p. 1411, Figure 1

D1.rationale: The allocation sequence was random (random number table, 1.1 Y) and baseline characteristics were balanced (1.3 N), but the report gives no information about allocation concealment (1.2 NI), which the algorithm maps to Some concerns. The inconsistent group sizes (n = 53 in the Abstract/Methods versus n = 54 in Table 1) slightly reinforces uncertainty about allocation and reporting, but no baseline imbalance suggesting a failed randomization was found.

D2.rationale: Carers could not be blinded (2.2 Y; 2.1 NI), but no deviations from the assigned PEEP-titration strategy arising from the trial context are reported (2.3 PN) and all randomized participants were analysed in their assigned groups (2.6 Y), so the algorithm yields Low risk for the effect of assignment. The minor discrepancy in the reported study-group size (53 vs 54) is not a deviation that would affect this judgement.

D3.rationale: Outcome data were available for all randomized participants: vital status is reported for all 51 control and 54 study participants at 60 days (Figure 1 numbers at risk), so 3.1 is Y and the conditional questions are NA.

D4.rationale: Outcome assessors were not blinded (4.3 Y), but all-cause mortality is an objective outcome that is unlikely to be influenced by knowledge of the assigned intervention (4.4 N), so 4.5 is NA and the domain is Low.

D5.rationale: No protocol, statistical analysis plan or registry record is available for this report, so 5.1 is NI; because analysis intentions are unavailable and mortality could have been measured and analysed in more than one eligible way (28-day versus 60-day, crude proportions versus time-to-event), 5.2 and 5.3 are also NI, giving Some concerns under the algorithm.

overall.rationale: Domains 2, 3 and 4 are Low, but Domain 1 (allocation concealment not described) and Domain 5 (no accessible pre-specified plan, with several eligible ways to measure and analyse mortality) raise some concerns; no domain is at high risk and the concerns do not jointly lower confidence sufficiently for a high-risk judgement, so overall Some concerns.

results.numerical_result: Duration of mechanical ventilation: mean 11.23 (SD 3.17) days in the study group vs 15.36 (SD 3.39) days in the control group; t = 6.451, P < 0.001
results.result_location: p. 1410, Table 5 (Prognostic analysis) and Section 3.5 'Prognostic analysis'

1.1.support: Random assignment of patients into either the control group or the study group was performed using a random number table.

1.2.support: The report describes only a random number table for sequence generation; I looked for any description of allocation concealment (sealed opaque envelopes, central or remote allocation) in the methods and found none.

1.3.support: They presented a homogeneous profile (all P > 0.05). Table 1 lists between-group P values of 0.426, 0.252, 0.234, 0.672, 0.216, 0.226 and 0.441 for the baseline characteristics.
1.3.location: p. 1409, Table 1 and Section 3.2 Baseline characteristics

2.1.support: I looked for any statement that participants were blinded to, or aware of, the assigned PEEP-titration strategy and found none; the report says only that both groups received sedation.

2.2.support: The study group underwent PEEP titration based on transpulmonary driving pressure. Esophageal pressure was measured as a surrogate for pleural pressure using an esophageal pressure measurement catheter connected to the ventilator; no blinding of carers or clinicians is described.

2.3.support: The report describes no deviations from the assigned PEEP-titration strategy, no crossovers between groups and no non-adherence in either group; I found no evidence that trial context changed what participants received.

2.4.support: Conditional on 2.3; 2.3 was answered PN, so this question is not applicable.

2.5.support: Conditional on 2.4; 2.4 was answered NA, so this question is not applicable.

2.6.support: In the study group, 15 patients died within 28 days, with a total of 14 cases of VAP. The duration of mechanical ventilation was (11.23 +/- 3.17) days; Table 5 reports this outcome for all 51 control and 54 study participants, with no exclusions described.

2.7.support: Conditional on 2.6; 2.6 was answered Y, so this question is not applicable.

3.1.support: Duration of mechanical ventilation is reported for all randomised participants - 51 in the control group (15.36 +/- 3.39 days) and 54 in the study group (11.23 +/- 3.17 days) - matching the randomised numbers, so no participant is missing this outcome.

3.2.support: Conditional on 3.1; 3.1 was answered Y, so this question is not applicable.

3.3.support: Conditional on 3.2; 3.2 was answered NA, so this question is not applicable.

3.4.support: Conditional on 3.3; 3.3 was answered NA, so this question is not applicable.

4.1.support: The outcome is days of mechanical ventilation taken from ventilator records; I found no indication that the measurement method is insensitive to plausible intervention effects or has poor validity.

4.2.support: I looked for any difference between the groups in the method, timing or intensity of measurement of ventilation duration and found none; the same records and the same 60-day follow-up were used for both groups.

4.3.support: No blinding of outcome assessors is described; the same clinical team adjusted the ventilator settings in the study group ('Adjustments were made 2-4 times per day') and recorded ventilation duration, so assessors knew the assigned strategy.

4.4.support: I looked for blinding of the clinical team or a protocolised, objective criterion defining the end of ventilation and found none; the same unblinded team adjusted ventilator settings 2-4 times per day, and the end of the measured duration is their decision to stop ventilation.

4.5.support: I found no report of a mechanism by which knowledge of allocation produced the recorded ventilation durations (for example a stated difference in weaning criteria or extubation practice between groups).

5.1.support: I looked for a trial protocol, statistical analysis plan or registry record, or any statement that the analysis plan was finalised before unblinded outcome data were available, and found none in the report.

5.2.support: Analysis intentions are not available, and duration of mechanical ventilation could have been measured in several eligible ways (for example ventilator-free days versus days of ventilation, or different time origins).

5.3.support: Analysis intentions are not available, and this measurement could have been analysed in multiple eligible ways (for example unadjusted t-test versus models accounting for participants who died while ventilated).

D1.rationale: The sequence was random (1.1 Y) and baseline characteristics were balanced (1.3 N), but allocation concealment is not described (1.2 NI), which the algorithm maps to Some concerns; the inconsistent study-group size across the report (53 vs 54) adds minor uncertainty.

D2.rationale: Carers were necessarily aware of the assigned strategy (2.2 Y; 2.1 NI), but no deviations arising from the trial context are reported (2.3 PN) and all randomized participants were analysed in their assigned groups (2.6 Y), giving Low risk under the algorithm for the effect of assignment.

D3.rationale: Ventilation duration is reported for all 51 control and 54 study participants (Table 5), so 3.1 is Y and the conditional questions are NA. Although deaths truncate the observable ventilation time, no missing outcome data are reported.

D4.rationale: Assessors were not blinded (4.3 Y), and the endpoint of this measurement - the decision to stop ventilation - was made by that unblinded team, so knowledge could have influenced the recorded duration (4.4 PY); there is no positive evidence that it did (4.5 PN), which the algorithm maps to Some concerns rather than High.

D5.rationale: No protocol, analysis plan or registry record is available (5.1 NI), and because analysis intentions are unavailable while the outcome can be defined and analysed in more than one eligible way, 5.2 and 5.3 are also NI; the algorithm gives Some concerns.

overall.rationale: Domain 1 (concealment not described), Domain 4 (unblinded determination of the end of ventilation) and Domain 5 (no accessible pre-specified plan) each raise some concerns while Domains 2 and 3 are Low. No domain is at high risk, and no single concern is sufficient on its own to make bias likely, so the overall judgement is Some concerns rather than High.
